the batch fermentation process of GSH production by Candidautilis WSH 02–08 can be controlled by the dissolved oxygen concentration, and the optimal dissolved oxygen concentration for GSH production is 35%.
the batch fermentation of glutathiones under constant DO concentrations of different level was more efficient in DCW and glutthione production than those under constant agitation rate.

DO concentration was the most important factor in the cultivation of Candida utilis W SH 02-08 and constant DO concentration of the fermentation process was better than constant agitation rate of the fermentation process in glutathione production.

the effect of DO concentration on the fermentation kinetics of glutathione by Candida utilis.
the analysis of batch fermentation process under different DO control modes and provides a theoretical basis for further optimization of the process.
the optimization of the fermentation conditions and provides a new approach for further study of the mechanism for glutathione production.

the increase of DO concentration was the key factor to enhance DCW and glutathi-one production in batch fermentation of glutathion by Candida utilis.
DO was one of the main factors influencing cell growth and product formation,and the control of DO was an effective method for the improvement of glutathione fermentation process.
constant DO concentration was more suitable for the fermentation process than constant agitation rate.

the increase of DCV and glutathione concentration under constant DO concentration was mainly attributed to the enhancement of the cell growth rate by the increase of oxygen transfer rate.
constant DO concentration of the fermentation medium is more effective in improving glutathione production than constant agitation rate.
DO was the key factor for glutathione production and DO control mode of 35% was more suitable for the strain than the constant agitation rate of fermentation.

the fermentation process of glutamine production in flasks can be controlled by the DO concentrations rather than the agitation rates.
